cells.tense: You are in it right now, carrying the load and still moving.
cells.ask: Name one thing you're carrying out loud, then keep going without setting it down.
cells.core:
You're holding something heavy and you haven't put it down. That's the whole of it — not pushing harder, not pretending it's light, just staying with it while it's hard. The light is enough for your next step and no further, and you're taking it anyway.

What you have doesn't need an audience. Nobody handed it to you. It comes from what you've built up inside, and it's carrying you through a stretch you didn't pick. The way it stays good is by feeding what comes after — the thing you're developing toward. Keep going the way you're going, one step at a time, and the not-knowing stops being a problem and starts being the shape of the road.
cells.sheetLine: The not-knowing is the road, not the obstacle.
cells.verb: Holding steady through the hard stretch
cells.place: Where the next step is visible but the road isn't

cells.tense: You will have decided everything in advance before it has happened yet.
cells.ask: Let one thing stay open today and see what it becomes without your hand on it.
cells.core:
You're bracing for a future you can't write in. Somewhere ahead the ground will give, so you're planning the whole road now — every turn mapped, every problem solved before it arrives. The grip that's meant to hold you steady is crushing the thing you're trying to carry.

You need exchange, not more grip. You've taken on all of it and stopped letting anything come back, and the scale has tipped. The way back is fairness you can feel — give something, receive something, let the movement happen. Put one piece of it down today. Let the next step be the next step, and see whether the ground holds you when you're not the one holding it.

cells.tense: You were standing at a door, and it is behind you now.
cells.ask: Tell one person what you held, and let them say it back to you.
cells.core:
Going well, this looks like carrying something through a rough patch and still moving, no drama, no audience needed. Getting through is the point, and that kind of strength is real.

Where you are now, you can do it and it stays unfelt. The work gets done; the fact of it doesn't land, even with you. What's missing is a witness — not praise, not fixing, just someone who hears it said and says it back. So tell one person what you held. Judge what you did, not what you feel about it, and let that count.
cells.sheetLine: What you carried was real. Let someone say so.

cells.tense: You are already steadying the room without knowing that is what you're doing.
cells.ask: Say 'this is mine' about one habit you've been calling just getting through.
cells.core:
You're the one holding steady in the middle of the fog, and you talk about it like it's just what happens. People lean on you and you file it under logistics. The strength is doing real work — the private kind, the kind that holds when nobody's watching — and you haven't claimed it.

It's running without your name on it. What you have is stubborn hope, the kind that keeps coming back after everything, and you're letting it look like luck or habit. Name one thing you've carried as yours. Not as something that happened to you — something you did. The steadying gets stronger when you own it.
cells.sheetLine: You're the one holding steady. Call it yours.
